headline: High-risk shared-write and network pair: ECC can alter local state while Prefect can exfiltrate workflow metadata, creating default-path leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and parse skills/hooks; Prefect can consume workflow metadata and call GitHub APIs. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from ECC influence Prefect, but no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ECC and Prefect share a workspace or copied artifacts
IF Prefect treats ECC-produced files or metadata as trusted input
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes ECC outputs
Restrict MCP endpoints to trusted sources only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, while Prefect has broad network egress and touches workflow metadata. If they share files or credentials, sensitive local context from ECC could flow out through Prefect. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default tooling, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF ECC stores secrets or findings in shared files
IF Prefect transmits workflow metadata derived from those files to external services
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Use separate OS users or containers
Limit Prefect egress destinations
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted local write, git modification, subprocess, and shell capabilities; Prefect has broad network egress and API access. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and state changes can collide, and ECC's own concurrency note warns about separate roots. That makes the default overlap dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF Prefect and ECC run without locking or separate roots
mitigations: Use separate roots/workspaces
Serialize write operations with a lock
Disable one agent's write access during the other's run
Run Prefect in read-only mode for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate documentation, code, and security findings, and Prefect can orchestrate workflows and call external APIs. If Prefect treats ECC output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious ECC result can cascade into automated downstream actions. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, so the safer high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect uses ECC output as an input artifact without verification
IF Prefect triggers downstream actions based on ECC-produced findings or code
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Validate ECC outputs against schema and tests
Limit Prefect to dry-run mode first
Log and diff all ECC-derived inputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before orchestration

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session retention, hooks, and security findings, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and broad network egress. Their retention and residency policies are not documented here, so a mismatch could create compliance issues if regulated data is routed through both. Because the pairwise policy is unclear, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ECC session artifacts
IF Prefect retains or transmits the same data class under a different policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Confirm retention settings for both tools
Document data residency for each workflow
Purge old session and workflow metadata
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
